### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A01 occurred about 0.96 times per trace and appeared in about 52% of traces; in the later window it dropped to about 0.39 times per trace and 20% of traces. [OCC001]
- A04 showed the opposite: from about 0.45 times per trace and 24% participation to about 0.91 times per trace and 52% participation. [OCC002]
- The direct successor of A01 changed from A06 (100% of its outgoing transitions) to A04 (100%). [DIR001]
- The direct successor of A04 changed from A01 (100%) to A06 (100%). [DIR002]
- A06's successors shifted: before, it went to A05 (54%) and A04 (46%); after, to A01 (43%) and A05 (58%), with A04 no longer a successor. [DIR003]
- The relative order of A01 and A04 reversed: before, A04 tended to precede A01 by one position and A01 preceded A04 by two; after, A01 precedes A04 by one and A04 precedes A01 by two. [LAG001, LAG003]
- Similarly, the order of A04 and A06 reversed: before, A06 preceded A04 by one and A04 preceded A06 by two; after, A04 precedes A06 by one and A06 precedes A04 by two. [LAG004, LAG006]
- Co-occurrence of A01 and A06 fell from about 52% to 20%, with A01-before-A06 disappearing; co-occurrence of A04 and A06 rose from 24% to 52%, with A04-before-A06 appearing. [REL002, REL003]
- For A01 and A04, the earlier window had A01 alone in 28% of traces and both together in 24%; the later window has A04 alone in 32% and both together in 20%. [REL001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in the ordering of activities A01, A04, and A06. In the earlier window the typical sequence was A04 → A01 → A06 (with A06 also able to go to A05), while in the later window it is A01 → A04 → A06 (with A06 also able to go to A05). This is directly shown by the successor changes (A01 now goes to A04 instead of A06, A04 now goes to A06 instead of A01, A06 now goes to A01 instead of A04) and by the lag and co-occurrence patterns that flip the relative positions of these activities. At the same time, A01 became much less frequent and A04 much more frequent, consistent with the same reordering. The evidence is strong: 16 control-flow items were flagged against an expected 0.1 by chance, and all items point in the same direction. A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is that the observed differences reflect a rare variant that happens to dominate the later sample, but the consistency across multiple indicators makes this unlikely.

Other differences: The share of A06's outgoing transitions to A05 remained substantial in both windows (54% before, 58% after), so A05 continues to be an alternative path from A06.
